source.title: Delving Deeper into Data Scaling in Masked Image Modeling
source.authors: Cheng Lu; Xiao-Jie Jin; Qibin Hou; J. Liew; Ming-Ming Cheng; Jia-Shi Feng

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices and references.
record.tranche_reason: Extends investigation of scaling to masked image modeling and image data, reporting downstream outcomes as pre-training data size changes; it does not test language-model pre-training loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The study reports downstream performance across pre-training data sizes, which bears on V6. It does not report held-out pre-training loss or fit loss power laws, test extrapolation from small runs, or evaluate compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. The results for different reconstruction targets and sampling strategies are reported, but only selected rows are included below; robustness tables are also not exhaustively extracted.
record.test_reason: The study reports downstream task performance of MAE-style masked-image-modeling ViTs (B/L/H) as random Coyo pre-training subsets grow from 0.5M to 100M images. This bears on V6 (downstream improvement with scale) in a new modality. It reports no pre-training loss, no power-law fits and no compute-optimal sweeps, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested. Caveat: epochs fall as data grows (300/300/300/90/15), so samples seen stay roughly 1–1.5B. The data axis is therefore unique-data growth at roughly fixed compute, not unbottlenecked scaling.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors conclude MIM data scalability is roughly limited to 10M images, and most downstream tasks saturate beyond that, even with stronger target encoders and harder tasks. LVIS (rare categories) is the exception. They also conclude stronger targets help but don't break saturation, and that sampling strategy is non-critical ('data-agnostic').
record.recipe_differences: Image-model masked-image-modeling experiments using downstream task metrics and web-collected image data; no language-model held-out loss fitting or compute-optimal allocation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with pre-training dataset size, model variant, downstream task, and data sampling strategy. The paper reports that CiT sampling does not materially change the overall scaling tendency.

fits_no_version.finding: Reconstruction-target choice changes downstream level and data gains: CLIP target gives larger gains IN1k→IN22K, and EVA-G/CLIP-L targets raise accuracy. Saturation beyond 10M persists regardless of target.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pre-training objective/target strength shifts the downstream scaling curve but not its saturation point.

fits_no_version.finding: CiT similarity-based data sampling leaves the data-scaling trend unchanged (ViT-L IN1k 86.20→86.22 at 10M→100M).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data curation does not alter downstream data-scaling saturation in MIM.

record.problems: The study reports downstream metrics rather than pre-training loss or fitted scaling laws. The authors note that configurations may be suboptimal, only MAE-style pre-training is tested, and model and dataset scales remain limited. No uncertainty estimates are given in the reported tables.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining Coyo-0.5M and Coyo-1M table values are omitted, as are additional target-encoder comparisons in Tables 1 and 8, CiT sampling-strategy comparisons in Table 5, and most robustness outcomes in Tables 9–11. These were omitted to prioritize selected larger-scale downstream comparisons, the reported saturation pattern, and the LVIS exception within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No held-out pre-training loss and no loss-vs-parameters/data/compute power-law fits.
No fixed-compute allocation of parameters vs data.
No shape comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Image modality is used, but no pre-training loss or power-law form is reported.
No functional fit or prediction from loss. Compute and samples seen were not held separate from data size. Language models are not tested.
No fitted exponents or fitting-choice comparisons.

missing.what: Model-size scaling at fixed data: ViT-H underperforms ViT-L at small data (IN1k FT 82.00 vs 82.18 at 0.5M). It also underperforms on ADE20K/CityScapes at all sizes (CityScapes 100M 81.51 vs 82.59).
Longer pre-training at 100M does not help: 10 vs 15 epochs with EVA-G target gives 86.90 vs 86.94.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Treated as V6 in a vision setting. A strict reading restricting V6 to language models would move this to fits_no_version. Key confound: epochs scale inversely with data (300/300/300/90/15), so samples seen are ~1.5B, 0.9B and 1.5B for 5M, 10M and 100M. The 'data scaling' is not at matched or increasing compute, and saturation may reflect compute or model bottleneck, as V1's 'other two not bottleneck' caveat anticipates. The large 0.5M→5M gains (e.g. ViT-B LP 31.77→71.70) are declared in rows_left_out but should be added; they are the clearest scaling evidence. No uncertainty estimates; single runs.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pre-training loss measurements or loss-versus-parameter, token, or compute power-law fits.
No predictions from small runs are compared with much larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep over parameter count and training tokens.
No comparison of depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.
The study concerns image models, but reports downstream performance rather than whether the same pre-training-loss power-law form holds in image models or other training regimes.
Tests downstream performance across image pre-training dataset sizes, not language-model downstream performance, predictions from pre-training loss, or performance as a function of compute.
No fitted loss exponents or compute-optimal splits are compared; downstream performance saturation is reported, not bending of a fitted pre-training-loss power law.

relationships.reason: Downstream metrics rise modestly from 5M to 10M on most tasks, e.g. ViT-H IN1k FT +0.29 and LP +0.45 (r03,r05,r07,r09,r11,r13,r17,r19,r23,r25,r27,r31,r33,r35).
relationships.display_finding: Most downstream metrics improved modestly, including ViT-H ImageNet fine-tuning by 0.29 and linear probing by 0.45.

relationships.condition: 10M→100M on ImageNet-1k/5k, COCO (most), ADE20K, at fixed model size and roughly fixed samples seen
relationships.reason: 10× more data gives negligible change (≤0.3 points, some declines), which the authors call saturation. Fewer epochs at 100M may mean the runs were compute-limited (r02,r04,r06,r08,r10,r12,r14,r18,r20,r24,r26,r28,r30,r42).
relationships.display_finding: Tenfold data growth changed scores by at most 0.3 points, sometimes downward, with fewer epochs potentially constraining the larger-data runs.

relationships.condition: 10M→100M on LVIS (esp. rare classes), CityScapes, some COCO ViT-L, iNat
relationships.reason: Gains continue: LVIS AP +0.98, rare-class AP +3.3, CityScapes ViT-H +1.05 (r16,r22,r32,r34,r36,r37,r38,r39,r41).
relationships.display_finding: Further gains included 0.98 LVIS AP, 3.3 rare-class AP, and 1.05 on CityScapes with ViT-H.

relationships.condition: 5M→10M on specific pairs (ViT-B IN1k FT, ViT-L COCO, ViT-H ADE20K, iNat)
relationships.reason: Metrics are flat or decline slightly. The iNat drop is attributed to more iterations at 5M, showing dependence on training length (r01,r15,r21,r29,r40).
relationships.display_finding: Scores stayed flat or declined slightly, with the iNat decline attributed to more training iterations in the 5M setting.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: Performance rises in many reported comparisons, including ViT-H ImageNet fine-tuning and linear probing and several COCO and segmentation results (r05, r11, r17, r23, r31, r35).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Some specific model and task comparisons from 5M to 10M
reader_labels.reason: Performance is not uniformly increasing: several values decrease slightly, including ViT-B ImageNet fine-tuning, ViT-L COCO AP box and mask, ViT-H ADE20K, and iNaturalist2018 (r01, r15, r21, r29, r40).
